what_happened: The command was RIGHT and the route went ahead-right, but the policy planned a path to the left and swung the ego across many lanes, away from the recorded path (13 m off). It ended up off the drivable area at 8.9 s, going about 5 m/s. No collision was recorded (collision_at_fault is 0 in the metrics), so this failure is the offroad.

On a multi-lane highway, after handoff the ego was told to go STRAIGHT and then RIGHT, but it steered left out of its lane. It kept turning left across the lanes beside it until it left the drivable area toward the left barrier at 6.9 s, about 3.3 m from the human path. The camera view was clean before the drift, and the metrics show offroad=1 with no recorded collision, so the failure is the policy steering off the road.

The command was RIGHT and the recorded path ran straight up the right lanes, but after handoff the policy steered left, cutting across the lanes at an angle toward the left road edge while slowing from 17 to 7 m/s. At 7.9 s it was at the edge, 11.6 m off the recorded path, and actor 32, driving along the road, hit its right side.

On a multi-lane highway with a RIGHT command, the policy steered left, away from the recorded path that heads right. It crossed the left road edge into the guardrail and median at about 5–7 m/s with no lead vehicle close by; the collision metrics stay at 0, so the failure is the offroad.

After handoff, the policy's planned path bent left even though the route command was STRAIGHT and then RIGHT. The ego slowed from about 18 to 11 m/s while drifting left across the lanes and onto the landscaped median before the intersection, ending up 7.3 m from the human's trajectory. No actors were nearby, and the camera view was clean until the ego was already in the bushes.

The ego was creeping up a queue of stopped traffic about 3 m left of where the recorded human drove. It slowed from 1.7 to 0.3 m/s but never fully stopped, and rolled its front into the stopped lead car 24 directly ahead, which was clearly visible in the camera.

In slow, dense highway traffic with a LEFT command, the ego didn't follow the recorded lane change to the left (it ended about 2.9 m off the recorded path). It stayed behind the slow grey van ahead (actor 13), closed in from 7.6 m to 4.3 m while only easing from 4.0 to 1.8 m/s, and hit the van's rear with its front at 8.3 s (a rear contact on the ego came later and didn't cause this).

On a straight multi-lane highway with a STRAIGHT command, the policy took over at 4.7s and steered right out of its lane toward the lane where actor 4 was. In doing so it cut into actor 3, which was driving alongside in that right lane, and hit it with its front at 6.4s. The front-camera smear only shows up at the moment of impact.
